about: Canvas `font` shorthands and what each sets. Read by tests/css_grammar.rs for the Rust font grammar and by tests/suite/css-grammar.test.js for `ctx.font`, so the two surfaces answer one table rather than two.
source: Chrome 152.0.7977.149: ctx.font set on a fresh 2D context after a sentinel font, then ctx.font, ctx.fontVariantCaps and ctx.fontStretch read back, measured 2026-10-22. A refused row is one Chrome ignored, leaving the sentinel. `font` is what ctx.font reads back by HTML, CSSOM section 6.7.2 and CSS Fonts 4 -- components in the grammar's order, a weight as its number, a width as its keyword, an `oblique` with its angle, numbers in their shortest form to six decimals, a family name as a quoted string and a generic as its keyword -- and `chrome`, where present, is what Chrome 152 read back instead; docs/browser-differences.md lists the differences. `parts` is the font Chrome's readback describes, taken apart; `lineHeight`, which Chrome does not expose, is CSS Fonts 4's: a number or percentage multiplies the size, `normal` is none. Relative sizes resolve against the canvas's default 10px font and `rem` against 16px, as Chrome does. Sizes are clamped to 10000px, as Chrome reads `20000px Arial`, and a computed negative size to zero; computed weights are held to 1 to 1000. For `oblique` with an angle, `parts.style` is the slant a `Font` takes rather than what Chrome reads back, which keeps the keyword only for the default 14deg: any angle but zero is `italic`, the oblique slant, and zero is `normal`. `font` keeps the angle written: `oblique 10deg`, and `oblique 0deg` too, a computed value of its own though it draws upright. An oblique draws by CSS Fonts 4's rule whatever the angle, and Chrome draws it otherwise; docs/browser-differences.md has both.
notMeasured: System-font keywords (caption, icon, menu, message-box, small-caption, status-bar) and `oblique 10deg 16px Arial` are left out: Chrome on macOS read every system font as 16px Arial, which is platform-specific, and serialized the oblique angle away.
knownDifferences: Measured and left out: a font size in `ex`, `ch` or `cap`, or in `rex`, `rch` or `rcap`, which Chrome resolves against 10px, or 16px for the root forms, of its standard family -- Times on macOS, so `1ex Oswald` is 4.4873px whatever family is named -- and which resolves here against the face `serif` resolves to, which differs by platform; `lh`, `rlh`, the viewport and container units, which Chrome resolves against the document and which read as zero here; and `16px "serif"` and `16px "inherit"`, which Chrome keeps quoted because a quoted generic or keyword names a family literally, and which a `Font` cannot tell from the unquoted name.

cases.css: normal normal normal normal normal 16px Arial
